name: Portland
note: Configuration for portland.html (the same engine as chicago.html). The geography comes from OpenStreetMap via tools/fetch-osm.py portland and tools/build-osm-city.py portland into portland-osm.json. This file holds landmark decorations and cards, the detailed street areas and viewpoints. Positions are [lat, lon]. The model is flat: the West Hills are not raised.

fetch._: the whole map is a detail zone: every building is kept

districts._: [name, hex colour, base height, tallest, box as [lat south, lon west, lat north, lon east]]

el._: MAX light rail and the Portland Streetcar run at grade on their mapped tracks

landmarks.name: U.S. Bancorp Tower
landmarks.info: 111 SW 5th Ave · 1983 · 166 m. 'Big Pink', for the pink granite and glass that glows at sunset.

landmarks.name: Wells Fargo Center
landmarks.info: 1300 SW 5th Ave · 1972 · 166 m, the tallest building in Oregon.

landmarks.name: KOIN Center
landmarks.info: 222 SW Columbia St · 1984 · 155 m. Brick and glass under a pointed blue roof.

landmarks.name: Park Avenue West
landmarks.info: 760 SW 9th Ave · 2016 · 152 m, finished years after its foundations sat as a hole in the ground through the recession.

landmarks.name: The Portland Building
landmarks.info: 1120 SW 5th Ave · 1982 · Michael Graves. The first major postmodern building; Portlandia kneels over the entrance.

landmarks.name: Pioneer Courthouse Square
landmarks.info: 'Portland's living room' · 1984 · a brick plaza stepped down like an amphitheatre, with the Weather Machine that forecasts at noon.

landmarks.name: Pioneer Courthouse
landmarks.info: 700 SW 6th Ave · 1875 · the oldest federal building in the Pacific Northwest, with its octagonal cupola.

landmarks.name: Powell's City of Books
landmarks.info: 1005 W Burnside St · the largest independent bookstore in the world, a full city block of colour-coded rooms.

landmarks.name: Union Station
landmarks.info: 800 NW 6th Ave · 1896 · the clock tower carries 'Go By Train' in neon.

landmarks.name: White Stag sign
landmarks.info: White Stag Building, Old Town · 1940 · the neon 'Portland Oregon' sign with its leaping stag, over the west end of the Burnside Bridge.

landmarks.name: Steel Bridge
landmarks.info: 1912 · a double-deck vertical-lift bridge: trains and MAX on the lower deck, cars and MAX above.

landmarks.name: Hawthorne Bridge
landmarks.info: 1910 · the oldest vertical-lift bridge in operation in the United States.

landmarks.name: Burnside Bridge
landmarks.info: 1926 · a double-leaf bascule bridge, the planned seismic lifeline across the river.

landmarks.name: Morrison Bridge
landmarks.info: 1958 · a bascule bridge whose leaves are among the longest of their kind.

landmarks.name: Broadway Bridge
landmarks.info: 1913 · a Rall-type bascule bridge, painted 'Golden Gate red'.

landmarks.name: Fremont Bridge
landmarks.info: 1973 · a tied-arch bridge, 116 m above the river at its crown.

landmarks.name: Marquam Bridge
landmarks.info: 1966 · the double-deck Interstate 5 crossing.

landmarks.name: Tilikum Crossing
landmarks.info: 2015 · 'Bridge of the People': a cable-stayed bridge for MAX, streetcars, buses, bikes and walkers, with no cars.

landmarks.name: Tom McCall Waterfront Park
landmarks.info: Built in 1978 where Harbor Drive, a freeway, used to run along the river.

landmarks.name: Salmon Street Springs
landmarks.info: Tom McCall Waterfront Park · 1988 · 185 jets that children run through on summer days.

landmarks.name: Mill Ends Park
landmarks.info: SW Naito Pkwy and Taylor St · the smallest park in the world, 61 cm across, in the median.

landmarks.name: Skidmore Fountain
landmarks.info: 1888 · the city's oldest piece of public art, beside the Saturday Market.

landmarks.name: Lan Su Chinese Garden
landmarks.info: 239 NW Everett St · 2000 · a walled Suzhou-style garden around a lake.

landmarks.name: Chinatown Gate
landmarks.info: NW 4th Ave and W Burnside St · 1986 · five roofs and two bronze lions.

landmarks.name: Vera Katz Eastbank Esplanade
landmarks.info: A 2.4 km path on the east bank, with a floating walkway on the river.

landmarks.name: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry
landmarks.info: 1945 SE Water Ave · the USS Blueback, the submarine from The Hunt for Red October, is moored beside it.

landmarks.name: Oregon Convention Center
landmarks.info: 777 NE MLK Jr Blvd · 1990 · the twin glass spires are lit at night.

landmarks.name: Moda Center
landmarks.info: 1 N Center Ct St · 1995 · home of the Trail Blazers.

landmarks.name: Veterans Memorial Coliseum
landmarks.info: 300 N Winning Way · 1960 · a glass box around the arena bowl.

landmarks.name: Providence Park
landmarks.info: 1844 SW Morrison St · 1926 · home of the Timbers and Thorns.

landmarks.name: Portland Aerial Tram
landmarks.info: 2006 · two cabins climb 150 m in four minutes from South Waterfront to OHSU on Marquam Hill (the model is flat, so the upper station stands on a tower).

landmarks.name: Portland Art Museum
landmarks.info: 1219 SW Park Ave · 1892 · the oldest art museum in the Pacific Northwest.

landmarks.name: Keller Fountain Park
landmarks.info: 1971 · Angela Danadjieva's waterfall fountain, meant to be walked on.

landmarks.name: International Rose Test Garden
landmarks.info: Washington Park · 1917 · more than 10,000 rose bushes; the reason Portland is the City of Roses.

landmarks.name: Portland Japanese Garden
landmarks.info: Washington Park · 1963 · five gardens on the hillside above the rose garden.

landmarks.name: Mount Hood
landmarks.info: 80 km east · 3,429 m, the highest point in Oregon. Shown at the right size for its distance.

landmarks.name: Mount St. Helens
landmarks.info: 85 km north-east · 2,549 m since the 1980 eruption took off its top.

terrain._: elevation grid spacing in metres; tiles from tools/fetch-terrain.py
